Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's president and CEO and left the board, effective immediately.
CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board looks for a permanent one. Nvidia gave no reason.
The stock fell more than 11% before the market opened.

paragraphs.text: Jensen Huang has resigned as president and chief executive of Nvidia, the company confirmed on Thursday, November 12, 2026, according to TechCrunch. Cointelegraph reported that he also gave up his seat on the board and that the resignation took effect immediately. Huang is a co-founder of Nvidia, Cointelegraph noted, and his exit ends the only leadership the chipmaker has had at the top during the AI boom.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO until a permanent successor is named, and she keeps her role as CFO, both outlets reported. According to Cointelegraph, the board is considering internal and external candidates for the permanent job.
When Jensen Huang resigned and what Nvidia said

A regulatory filing cited by TechCrunch says the board accepted Huang's resignation on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, one day before the public announcement. In its statement the company thanked Huang for his contributions to Nvidia and to the industry, TechCrunch reported.

The board also named Harvey Jones as its chair. He is the managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and a former chief executive of Synopsys, and he has been an Nvidia director since 1993, according to TechCrunch. Both outlets describe him as the first chair the board has had.
Why Jensen Huang resigned: Nvidia gave no reason

Neither report gives a reason for the resignation, and neither quotes Huang. The departure follows several days of damaging headlines. TechCrunch wrote that Huang had admitted to a romantic affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, and described the episode as having set off a national security crisis in the United States. Cointelegraph pointed to a Wall Street Journal report, published before the resignation, that Nvidia was preparing to oust him. TechCrunch also listed further claims in its related coverage, including an accusation of a second relationship inside the company and a race among law firms to sue Nvidia; this article does not rely on those claims.

Investors reacted before the market opened. Nvidia shares fell more than 11 percent in premarket trading on Thursday, according to TechCrunch, which added that the stock had already dropped sharply over the previous days and that the company had lost more than $300 billion in market value.
Who runs Nvidia now: Colette Kress as interim CEO

For now the company is run by a finance chief doing two jobs at once. Kress remains CFO and executive vice president while serving as interim CEO, TechCrunch reported, and the search for a permanent chief covers candidates inside and outside the company, according to Cointelegraph.

NeuraFeed's reading: this is one of the biggest leadership changes the AI industry has faced. Nvidia's chips sit under nearly every major AI model, and for three decades the company's strategy and its public voice were the same person. An interim CEO who is also the CFO signals that the board moved quickly and without a successor ready. The appointment of a first chair suggests directors want more distance between the board and whoever runs the company next. Customers and rivals will read the choice of a permanent CEO as a statement about whether Nvidia keeps its current course.
Watch for the board's choice of a permanent CEO and whether it comes from inside Nvidia, and for Huang's own first public statement, which neither report includes.
